title: Renewal age and size structured numerical methods

items.title: Linear age-structured renewal transport problem
items.statement: Fix a finite horizon and nonnegative bounded Lipschitz mortality and fertility rates. The density solves n_t+n_a=-mu(a)n on a>0 with renewal inflow n(t,0)=integral beta(a)n(t,a) da and nonnegative L1 initial density.

items.title: Size transport with a nonlocal division kernel
items.statement: On size x>=0, specify nonnegative bounded Lipschitz growth g with g>=g_min>0, mortality mu, division-removal rate gamma, and a finite positive daughter-size kernel K_y supported on [0,y]; define the transport, absorbing upper outflow and exact zeroth/first kernel moments.

items.title: Characteristic formula and Volterra solution for age renewal transport
items.statement: Construct the unique nonnegative L1 mild solution by the characteristic formula and its scalar Volterra birth-rate equation on every bounded time interval.

items.title: Finite-volume size transport with positive division quadrature
items.statement: Advance cell masses with positive upwind size fluxes, total loss mu+gamma and a nonnegative discrete daughter-kernel matrix whose column moments are recorded; use an absorbing upper boundary and the variable-speed transport-plus-loss CFL.

items.title: Age-cohort quadrature along exact characteristics
items.statement:
Input a finite horizon $T>0$, a time step $\Delta t>0$, an age cutoff $A>0$, bounded nonnegative rates $\mu,\beta$ on $[0,A]$, and a finite positive initial quadrature $(a_i,m_i^0)_{i=1}^I$ supported in $[0,A)$ for the initial age measure on that interval. Set $N=\lfloor T/\Delta t\rfloor$; the procedure returns levels at $t_k=k\Delta t$ for $0\le k\le N$, with final time $N\Delta t\le T$. One option, when a nonnegative real-valued initial density $n_0$ is evaluable at every point of $[0,A]$, is to choose any finite partition $0=b_0<\cdots<b_I=A$ and apply [[alg-composite-midpoint-rule]] with $n=1$ separately on each cell $[b_{i-1},b_i]$: set $\Delta a_i=b_i-b_{i-1}$, $a_i=(b_{i-1}+b_i)/2$, and $m_i^0=Q_M(n_0;b_{i-1},b_i,1)=\Delta a_i\,n_0(a_i)$ for $1\le i\le I$. The cell widths need not be equal. A cohort at age $a_i^k$ and mass $m_i^k$ follows the exact age characteristic

$$a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+\Delta t$$

and updates its survival mass by forward Euler,

$$m_i^{k+1}=(1-\Delta t\,\mu(a_i^k))m_i^k.$$

If $\Delta t\|\mu\|_\infty>1$, return status invalid-step with no updates. Otherwise initialize the birth and outflow records as empty and set $\nu_h^0=\sum_i m_i^0\delta_{a_i^0}$. For each $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, first calculate $B_h^k=\sum_i\beta(a_i^k)m_i^k$. Advance every existing cohort by $a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+\Delta t$ and update its survival mass by $m_i^{k+1}=(1-\Delta t\mu(a_i^k))m_i^k$. If an updated age is at least $A$, record that updated mass as discrete outflow and discard the cohort; otherwise retain it. Then insert a newborn cohort of age $0$ and mass $\Delta t B_h^k$ at time $t_{k+1}$. Record $B_h^k$ and the step's outflow, and form $\nu_h^{k+1}$ from the retained cohorts and this newborn. A failed rate evaluation returns failure with no partial update. The procedure returns the finite sequence $(\nu_h^k)_{k=0}^N$ and its birth/outflow records. The bounded-Lipschitz quadrature defect of the initial measure and the Euler survival error are separate inputs to any consistency claim.

items.title: Finite-age renewal model with absorbing outflow
items.statement: Restrict the age renewal transport model to [0,A], retain mortality and renewal births over [0,A], and absorb each cohort reaching age A; for A>T no birth cohort reaches the cutoff during the horizon.

items.title: Positive age-renewal evolution and L1 data stability
items.statement: The linear renewal solution operator is positive and has L1 norm at most exp(beta_max t); differences in initial densities and bounded mortality/fertility perturbations satisfy an explicit finite-horizon L1 bound.

items.title: Size characteristics, positivity, and discrete number and size-moment balances
items.statement: Under the size transport-plus-loss CFL and nonnegative kernel quadrature, cell masses stay nonnegative and satisfy exact discrete number and weighted-size balance identities, including growth, mortality, parent removal, division and boundary outflow terms.

items.title: Characteristic solution and mass bound for the finite-age renewal model
items.statement: The absorbing finite-age model has a unique characteristic/Volterra solution, exponential mass bound, and explicit cumulative initial-cohort outflow.

items.title: Positive composite or capped-adaptive quadrature for renewal births
items.statement: On each age cell, evaluate the nonnegative fertility times piecewise-constant density with positive composite-midpoint weights or capped adaptive-Simpson weights; return the estimate, indicator and explicit failure/cap status.

items.title: Weak consistency of age-cohort characteristic quadrature
items.statement: For C1 bounded rates and finite-horizon data with a bounded-Lipschitz initial quadrature defect, the cohort measure converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance at O(dt+initial-quadrature-defect), with birth-time quadrature, Euler survival and age-tail errors kept separate.

items.title: Finite-volume upwind scheme for age renewal transport
items.statement: For a finite age cutoff, uniform age cells, a positive birth quadrature and the transport-plus-loss CFL, update cell masses by explicit upwind flux, mortality and a specified absorbing right outflow.

items.title: Positivity, L1 growth and data stability of the renewal finite-volume step
items.statement: Under the transport-plus-loss CFL, the upwind mass update is nonnegative, grows by at most 1+dt beta_max per step, and is L1 stable for two data sets with a forcing term for coefficient or quadrature perturbations.

items.title: First-order finite-volume convergence for compatible smooth renewal data
items.statement: On a bounded horizon, for a C2 characteristic solution with compatible inflow data, comparable time and age steps satisfying the CFL, and true birth-quadrature defect O(da), the L1 cell-mass error is O(da+dt).

items.title: L1 convergence for BV data without renewal-boundary compatibility
items.statement: For nonnegative BV intersect L1 initial data and bounded Lipschitz nonnegative rates, the positive upwind scheme converges in L1 on every bounded horizon without imposing corner compatibility; this is a convergence result, with no smooth Taylor rate claimed.

items.title: Age-cutoff survival, outflow and infinite-age tail bounds
items.statement: For A>T, newborn cohorts do not reach the cutoff during [0,T]; outflow is bounded by the initial tail above A-T, and the finite-cutoff model differs from the infinite-age solution by at most 2 exp(beta_max T) times that tail, separately from discretization error.

title: Renewal age and size structured numerical methods — Examples

items.title: A narrow maturation kernel approaches a delayed birth term
items.statement: For a normalized triangular fertility kernel centered at a positive age, prove an O(epsilon) convolution-to-delay bound for Lipschitz birth histories and state explicitly why finite width is not an exact delay equation.

items.title: Half-size division preserves the discrete biomass budget
items.statement: For three parent cohorts of size 2, remove each parent and create two daughters of size 1 in one exact division step; verify the number increase and exact weighted-size conservation.

items.title: Constant mortality with age-localized fertility
items.statement: For constant mortality, a triangular fertility profile supported on ages [1,2], and initial density 1 on [1,2], compute the birth trace, the initial compatibility defect and the first positive finite-volume birth update.

items.title: A longer run exposes age-cutoff outflow error
items.statement: For zero mortality and fertility with initial density exp(-a), compute exact cutoff and outflow losses on a unit upwind grid and show how the tail error grows as the simulated horizon approaches the finite cutoff.
